sectors.title: High-redshift galaxy kinematics
sectors.new_work: Recomputed 73 KMOS3D, 21 KGES and 169 KROSS objects at three radii, under constant a₀, reference H tracking and the newly fitted exponential cosmology; repeated resolved-object cuts.
sectors.result: For KMOS3D outer radii, the log-acceleration residual slope is −0.245 dex per unit redshift with constant a₀ and −0.313 with the common H(z) law. The latter has median log-velocity residual −0.087 dex. The new cosmology does not remove this trend. The reference z=2.3 example gives boosts approximately 2.02 versus 1.39.
sectors.scope: These are catalogue central-value diagnostics using the supplied radius-dependent baryon force models, not raw-cube likelihoods. The 112-point reference projection has intercept 1.002784 and slope 1.225645; it is not the sample-weighted MUSE regression. Main-text halo and Appendix-E MOND inferences must remain separate.
sectors.remaining: Exact MUSE 79-object selection, MOND fit products/covariance and resolved baryon/pressure-support likelihoods are still needed. No new JWST forward fit was completed. The full numerical C03-163 and composed C03-165 Lean statements remain open.

sectors.title: CMB-to-galaxy normalization
sectors.new_work: Recomputed the bare, formation-mass and surviving-stock distinctions; tied the actual cosmology fit to the galaxy normalization.
sectors.result: Bare 1/ε = 5.320685; the fitted formation convention uses 5.333. H₀ = 68.939 implies a₀ = 1.2588e-10 m s⁻². This is about 2.3% above the H₀=67.4 reference value, with no new a₀ fit.
sectors.scope: The exact reciprocal identity is a pre-release, bare-normalization statement. A mass-convention factor and survival factor multiply its corrected version. Planck-inferred abundance and H₀ are model-dependent and correlated; galaxy mass calibration makes the elementary empirical cross relation roughly a 20% test.
sectors.remaining: Independent phase-loading/normalization evidence and an explicit discovery-history account remain necessary for a strong one-constant evidential claim.

sectors.title: Local RAR and baryonic Tully–Fisher
sectors.new_work: Profiled distances, inclinations and stellar mass-to-light ratios for 130 SPARC galaxies and 2,710 points, then tested the common a₀, flow-distance rescaling and a 5 km/s velocity floor. Also evaluated 100 flat-speed BTFR entries.
sectors.result: The common-a₀ penalized score is 11258.0; with the velocity floor it is 3433.2. Median velocity χ² per point is 1.54; some galaxies dominate the sum. The reference BTFR median log-velocity residual is 0.020 dex, RMS 0.067 dex.
sectors.scope: The exponential shape was motivated by these data. The calculation applies the algebraic law to disk mass models and uses diagonal velocity errors; it is not a full nonspherical field solution or marginalized evidence. The normalization scan prefers smaller values within the tested range, but no global free-a₀ optimum was established.
sectors.remaining: A defensible joint distance, stellar-population and correlated-motion likelihood is needed before assigning significance to the normalization residuals.

sectors.title: Galaxy weak lensing
sectors.status: Updated summary agrees; reduction sensitivity demonstrated
sectors.new_work: Downloaded the Brouwer/KiDS release and full covariance, evaluated isolation cuts and morphology splits, then separately evaluated Mistele’s updated Table 1.
sectors.result: The updated table gives a reference-normalization diagonal score 10.06 over 15 bins when its tabulated statistical and interpolation/extrapolation errors are combined; 5.99 over the seven conservative inner bins. The older reduction has appreciable normalization and morphology residuals.
sectors.scope: The later analysis changes isolation, baryonic masses and deprojection and removes the reported type split. These are two reductions of overlapping data. Table errors are not a supplied full covariance; the lens redshift distribution and published H₀=73 calibration were not jointly refit. No calibrated p-value is assigned.
sectors.remaining: A common-cosmology raw-lens fit and a predicted retained-stock profile remain open. No-slip alone does not predict either profile or morphology dependence.

sectors.title: CMB acoustic peaks
sectors.status: New fit and ACT comparison completed, conditionally
sectors.new_work: Replaced linear depletion by exponential positive allocation in the existing geodesic perturbation pipeline, optimized five cosmological parameters, checked reference-fluid splits and numerical accuracy, and downloaded/evaluated ACT DR6-lite.
sectors.result: Planck-lite TTTEEE + BAO + DES SN: χ²=2227.80, matched ΛCDM 2228.32; Δχ²=-0.52. On ACT’s 135 bins, fixed cosmology with calibration profiling gives 162.73 versus 162.02. The official ACT scoring method independently reproduces the implementation to numerical precision.
sectors.scope: This tests acoustic spectra, not just an abundance ratio. Both models use massless neutrinos, linear lensing and A_lens=1. Conditional parameter counts 5 versus 6 give ΔAIC≈−2.52; this is not a Bayes factor or strong preference. Absolute scores move slightly with CAMB accuracy, while Δχ² changes by only about 0.005.
sectors.remaining: A joint ACT/Planck treatment needs the official overlap cuts/covariance, foreground treatment and broader parameter exploration. No SPT likelihood was run. This fit does not include the alternative scalar receiver for nonlinear exhaustion.

sectors.title: Growth and projected Weyl power
sectors.status: New ACT lensing test; full-shape growth open
sectors.new_work: Exported linear Weyl spectra and applied the official ACT DR6 lens-only bandpowers, covariance, bin windows and Hartlap correction, with a higher-accuracy lensing calculation.
sectors.result: Across 10 lensing bins, χ²=16.21 for release and 17.86 for the matched ΛCDM baseline. Raising lensing accuracy changes the release bandpowers by at most 0.013%.
sectors.scope: The observable is Weyl power: CAMB’s ordinary delta_tot does not include the dust placed in the bookkeeping fluid. A naïve sigma₈ from that variable would depend on the arbitrary reference split. Linear lensing is used for both models; nonlinear corrections are not established.
sectors.remaining: DESI full-shape clustering, survey-window convolution, galaxy bias/RSD and nonlinear weak-lensing likelihoods are not completed by this check.

sectors.title: Dark-energy history and distances
sectors.status: Common background refit completed; local exhaustion open
sectors.new_work: Reoptimized the release-history gate with exponential allocation and recalculated the timing and equation-of-state summaries.
sectors.result: ρΛ(2)/ρΛ(0)=0.968240; half the present vacuum lies at z=7.928, not z≈6 for this saved release history. The drain since z=1 is 0.4935% of initial comoving stock. The effective bookkeeping vacuum w today is -1.000540; intrinsic vacuum pressure remains p=−ρ.
sectors.scope: An interacting-vacuum effective w is not the same parameter as today’s CPL w₀. The direct BAO/SN fit is the relevant check and does not show a simple sign exclusion. The fitted history remains an input, not a uniquely derived local mixing law.
sectors.remaining: Uniform drain can exhaust local underdensities. The separate positive scalar-receiver construction avoids this conditionally but has extra matching choices and different perturbations; it has not been substituted into this fit. Pantheon+ and Union3 were not separately refit here.

sectors.title: Relaxed and colliding clusters
sectors.status: Budget audit completed; conservative map prediction open
sectors.new_work: Recomputed all 24 archived X-COP aperture budgets using the formation-mass convention and exponential survival, and reconciled them with the existing reciprocity audit.
sectors.result: Full cohort release leaves stock/baryon=5.1761; a coextensive cohort has baryon fraction 0.1619. Lower present aperture fractions require differing baryon/stock retention, not an automatic violation of the cohort budget.
sectors.scope: The old unequal-active-weight, universal-passive-mass interaction is not a closed momentum-conserving merger model. Conservative inertial stock can repair the dynamics, but the old phase-weight fit is not automatically a fit of the repaired theory. A response weight is not the same quantity as stock mass.
sectors.remaining: A conservative gas+stock merger evolution with specified initial conditions, followed by an actual lens-map likelihood, remains to be done. Bullet/CLASH map predictions cannot honestly be scored as passed. No independent RAR halo may be added on top of the full stock excess.

sectors.title: Gravitational slip and E_G
sectors.status: New transfer prediction compared with data
sectors.new_work: Computed E_G directly from the Weyl potential and baryon velocity divergence, checked the ΛCDM normalization including its baryon/total-density transfer ratio, and compared with ACT–BOSS summaries.
sectors.result: The release prediction is E_G=0.4375 at z=0.316 and 0.3862 at z=0.555, nearly scale independent over k=0.005–0.15 Mpc⁻¹. ACT–BOSS reports 0.49 (+0.14/−0.11) and 0.31 (+0.06/−0.05), respectively; neither comparison is a significant discrepancy.
sectors.scope: Equality of the two potentials is insufficient to fix this statistic: velocity growth and source normalization also enter. The calculation is at effective redshifts and assumes unbiased large-scale velocity tracing.
sectors.remaining: A joint window-convolved clustering/lensing likelihood, including the observational compression assumptions, is still needed.

sectors.title: Wide binaries and the Solar System
sectors.status: Null benchmarks checked; raw catalogue test open
sectors.new_work: Recomputed the smooth-tide scaling over 10–30 kAU and 1–2 solar masses and checked the zero-quadrupole benchmark against the latest Cassini estimate.
sectors.result: For Ω=28 and A=15 km s⁻¹ kpc⁻¹, the illustrative radial-tide speed effect ranges from about 1.1×10⁻⁵ to 6.0×10⁻⁴. Therefore ≤10⁻⁴ is not a universal bound across that separation range. Q₂=0 differs from the published Cassini central value by 0.89σ.
sectors.scope: The tide is ordinary environmental gravity. The distinctive commitment is no large extra internal MOND-like force for nested resolved systems. Carrier assignment and the local projection rule are physical assumptions. Current wide-binary analyses disagree and were not converted into a joint verdict.
sectors.remaining: A fixed-selection Gaia likelihood with projection, eccentricity, unresolved multiplicity, contamination and selection effects has not been run; future-release predictions are recorded locally, not externally preregistered.

sectors.title: Newton’s constant and lepton masses
sectors.new_work: Downloaded current CODATA tables, recomputed with high precision, reran the routing integer scan and all 43 Farey candidates, and retained the earlier formula-menu audit.
sectors.result: G*=6.6742890813e-11 (−0.073 CODATA σ); muon ratio pull -0.535σ; tau mass 1776.918782 MeV against 1776.93±0.09. Only n=7 survives the stated 401-integer, 2σ routing scan; only 2/7 survives the stated Farey, 1σ tau scan.
sectors.scope: These are precise conditional matches. g’s historical connection to G and the development of the marked formula after residuals were known prevent a blind-prediction interpretation. Finite-menu uniqueness does not define a probability over theories. The electron-calibrated G* and a measured native-ensemble G_R are different checks.
sectors.remaining: The look-elsewhere objection is not eliminated by proving the selected formula. A constrained action/matching argument or a genuinely prospective observable is needed; no demand for a maximal microscopic derivation is imposed here.

sectors.title: Gravitational waves and Lorentz tests
sectors.status: Public null benchmark reproduced; tensor completion open
sectors.new_work: Downloaded the GWTC-4.0 polarization data and reproduced the official combination of pre-O4a and O4a log Bayes factors; checked the GW170817 speed interval and the existing CDT campaign status.
sectors.result: Pure scalar and pure vector alternatives are disfavored relative to tensor polarization in the released combined benchmark. Mixed tensor-plus-extra-mode alternatives remain much less tightly distinguished. A luminal, tensor-only continuum prediction is compatible with these results.
sectors.scope: The benchmark cannot distinguish this model from GR. The archived CDT tensor chains failed equilibration; their sealed science payload was not opened or counted as a detection. Scalar Lean results do not prove the graviton or photon/matter Lorentz sector.
sectors.remaining: An equilibrated tensor measurement and a specified dispersion/polarization/particle-propagation operator map are needed for actual Crab, GRB and GW predictions. No new strain-level likelihood or O5 analysis was run.

sectors.title: Milky Way, LMC, streams and halo tilt
sectors.status: Existing live realizations consolidated; joint fit open
sectors.new_work: Reconciled the older aligned-halo failure with the later tilted-stock run, both independent phase replicas and the stock/director bridge; retained the archived MW/LMC normalization concerns.
sectors.result: Across the three 8-Gyr realizations, late halo tilts are 39.584–42.356° and stellar tilts 21.378–22.332°. This demonstrates repeatable conditional retention at the tested particle count. Late precession and rounding persist; a stationary continuum configuration has not been shown.
sectors.scope: The aligned and tilted branches are different commitments. The later feasibility result does not erase the aligned branch’s failure or supply a population distribution. The older halo-shape evidence ratio depends strongly on the chosen ΛCDM shape prior and inter-study errors.
sectors.remaining: A single conservative MW/LMC/stream/tilt fit with the same stock and force model is still required; the archived MW masses at 50 kpc are too high relative to the cited constraint. No new long N-body run was needed merely to repeat already stored realizations.

sectors.title: Dwarf satellites and tidal inheritance
sectors.status: Archived grid reanalysis completed; strong model dependence
sectors.new_work: Re-evaluated the saved moving-LMC satellite integrations with 10%, 20% and 30% model uncertainty, keeping both cuspy-halo prior widths.
sectors.result: Antlia 2 stock/NFW evidence rises from 0.007–0.019 at 10% uncertainty to 0.69–0.74 at 30%. Crater II falls from roughly 2.6×10⁵–2.0×10⁸ to 94–155. These shifts expose how much of the headline odds come from the restricted grid and uncertainty model.
sectors.scope: The old grid does not implement the new conservative joint-stock force closure and does not span cored or broader ΛCDM histories. Its odds are not multiplied into an overall score. Near-Newtonian tidal dwarfs are compatible with conventional tidal formation too; disequilibrium obstructs a clean gravity test.
sectors.remaining: Updated astrometry, common MW/LMC fitting, conservative tidal evolution and a derived carrier/phase boundary are needed before claiming unique satellite or tidal-dwarf predictions.

sectors.title: Old-disk vertical gravity
sectors.new_work: Reused the archived reduced vertical solver for NGC 6946 and NGC 628 at a₀=1.20, 1.2307 and 1.2588 ×10⁻¹⁰ m s⁻².
sectors.result: At the common-fit a₀, NGC 628’s completion fit has χ²≈2.04 for five dispersions and a −0.21σ radial/vertical mass offset; the algebraic QUMOND comparison has χ²≈8.95 and −2.91σ. The small normalization change preserves the earlier pattern.
sectors.scope: The QUMOND treatment is approximate and the NGC 628 gas profile and inclination introduce real uncertainty. A maximal disk plus a round conventional halo has similar vertical gravity, so this is not an independent rejection of ΛCDM.
sectors.remaining: The broader old-population disk programme needs separated stellar tracers, scale-height uncertainties and full nonspherical comparisons. Existing registered per-galaxy predictions are preserved.
